prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1290; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officer responded to a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in the travel lane when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the rear of the stopped vehicle. Driver 2 reported pain in the right shoulder and was evaluated at the scene. The nature of the impact and the forces involved are consistent with the injury Driver 2 described. Driver 1 and Driver 2 both confirmed that Passenger was riding in Driver 1's vehicle at the time, and the statements of both parties agree on this point. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle and the front of Driver 2's vehicle, and the visible damage is largely in line with the reported impact. No prior damage to either vehicle was noted by the parties or observed by the officer. No independent witnesses were identified at the scene. Driver 2 stated that Driver 2 lives with the policyholder, Driver 1, in the same household. Both vehicles were driven from the scene, and no citations were issued at this time pending further review.
